turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: Certainly! In many cultures, menstrual products are discussed privately within families, often by older females passing on knowledge and products to younger ones. This can happen through direct instruction or by showing how to use products. Cultural taboos sometimes make these conversations more secretive, which can limit open dialogue and access to information. In some communities with limited resources, women might rely on community support networks or traditional remedies to manage their periods.
